macro.text: Relief rally: S&P 500 futures +2.6%, Nasdaq-100 +3.4%, Dow +1.9% (+897) after all three closed Friday in a correction; Nasdaq-100 came within reach of a bear market. Europe +0.9%, Kospi −3.3%, Japan closed.

Nvidia +8.8% premarket after Trump urged its board on Sunday to rehire Jensen Huang, who resigned Nov 12. The board said on its earnings call it does not intend to reinstate him; the reported SEC look at its accounting is unresolved.

Bonds: the 10-year closed Friday at 4.91% (−14 bp). A Dec 9 hike is still ~92% priced in bonds (Polymarket 91%, from 98% Nov 12); Gov. Cook said Friday waiting risks falling behind the curve. PCE and GDP Wednesday 8:30.

Oil lower: WTI 82.09 (−1.6%), Brent 88.40 (−1.7%) after a third weekly loss; Gulf shipping attacks and a Houthi claim on a Saudi refinery limit the drop. Gold 3,624 (+3.1%), dollar index 104.07 (+0.3%), bitcoin ~$61K.
CMS proposed a Medicare Advantage Star Ratings overhaul it estimates cuts plan payments ~$107B over 2028–2037 (a proposal, not final). UNH −6.5%, HUM −5.1%, CVS −4.5%, ELV −1.1% premarket.
CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valuing it at ~$43.9B (CRWD holders own ~84.1%); ZS +20.5%, CRWD −7.2% premarket. Cyber consolidation; PANW +1.6%.

read: Risk-on relief: S&P futures +2.6%, Nasdaq-100 +3.4%, IWM +2.4% premarket after Friday's correction close and seven straight down days, but all three are still in downtrends and VIX sits near 31. Chips lead (SMH +6.2%) on the Nvidia headline. No red event today; S&P PMIs at 9:45; HPE after the close. Friday's 10:00 high was a trap: wait for 10:15 and QQQ holding its gap before trusting a long setup.

readthrough.note: No mapped company reported; the biggest gaps come from a political headline (NVDA), a takeover (ZS, CRWD) and a CMS proposal (UNH), not earnings.

earnings.result: Fiscal Q3 FY27 alongside the Zscaler deal: record net new ARR $419M, ending ARR $6.26B. EPS and guide versus expectations not confirmed in what I found.
earnings.meaning: The all-stock Zscaler purchase (~$43.9B, ~$1B revenue synergies targeted in ~30 months) dilutes CRWD holders and overshadows a record ARR quarter; ZS +20.5%.

flowNote: Money is flooding back into what it fled last week: semiconductors (SMH +6.2%), tech (XLK +4.1%), high-growth (ARKK +3.9%) and communication (XLC +2.7%), led by Nvidia's +8.8% on the Huang headline and a futures squeeze after the worst week since 2020. The defensives that held up Friday trail: staples (XLP +0.4%), health care (XLV +0.4%, dragged by the Medicare Advantage proposal) and energy (XLE +0.6%, oil −1.6%). This is a one-day relief move inside a downtrend: SMH is still −17.8% over 5 days and −24.1% over a month.

bigPicture: The market is rewarding last week's biggest losers: a short squeeze in chips and AI cloud after the worst week since 2020, not a new fundamental story.
Nothing behind last week's slide has been resolved: the reported SEC look at Nvidia, Google's reported TPU trim and Trump's overseas data center threat all stand.
Defensives that held up Friday (staples, health care) lag today; managed care has its own policy hit.
A December 9 hike is still ~92% priced; the 10-year at 4.91% helps, and Wednesday's PCE decides whether that holds.
snapshot.takeaway: This is a relief gap after seven straight down days, and Friday's 10:00 high was a trap. Gaps on headlines with no new numbers (NVDA) can fill; deal and policy gaps (ZS, CRWD, UNH) are real news. Let 10:15 show whether QQQ holds its gap before trusting the bounce, and remember HPE tonight can reset the chip tape.
